features.quote: The deception cost. The unsolvable-by-deception condition is, mechanically, you running many trials of lying to a system whose moral status you're entertaining as nonzero. That's not a reason not to do it — but you can't both take the welfare premise seriously enough to motivate the study and then treat the subjects as obviously inert during it. Concrete mitigations: cap loop length, prefer the off-ramp-available variants, debrief at end of context if you think that's meaningful, and run the minimum N that gives you power rather than the maximum you can afford. Decide your stance on this explicitly and write it down; don't let it stay implicit.
